Samantha, thanks — good questions. High level answers below; attaching a 1-pager with data extracts and an example export.

1) Measurement approach
- We compute uptime at a 1-minute resolution from our ingestion pipeline (request-level telemetry + health probes).
- We publish both aggregated SLO windows (1h/24h/30d) and a CSV export of the underlying minute-level series for independent verification.
- Aggregates are the canonical values for contractual SLOs; raw exports are for customer audits.

2) Alerting ownership
- Redwood owns platform-level alerts that indicate model-serving degradation (e.g., node failures, kernel OOM, inference error spike). Those are paged to our infra on-call.
- Customer-side alerts (integration-specific errors, client-side latency spikes due to network) are expected to be handled by the customer; we can provide webhook alert endpoints and recommended alert thresholds.
- For hybrid cases (e.g., sustained 99.9->99.5 availability drop), we trigger a combined incident bridge and loop in both teams.

3) Temporary metric access (2-week window)
- We can provide read-only Grafana viewer access scoped to your tenancy and a one-time CSV export of minute-series for the requested 30-day lookback.
- Data delivery: shared Drive link within 48 hours of approval; Grafana invite within 24 hours.

Attached: redwood-slo-extract.pdf (sample export)

If this covers procurement's needs, I can issue the temporary access and add it to the MSA as an appendix.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Grafana viewer role will be limited: no dashboard editing, no alert creation, and only the dashboards tied to your tenancy.
- For the combined incident flow we referenced: we'll include a runbook link and a pager escalation matrix in the MSA appendix.
